passages.text: There was a man in the land of Uz whose name was Job. And this man was blameless and upright, fearing God and shunning evil.
passages.sermon:
Job lived in the land of Uz.
Job was a man.
Job was blameless.
Job was upright.
Job feared God.
Job shunned evil.
passages.original: אִ֛ישׁ הָיָ֥ה בְאֶֽרֶץ־ ע֖וּץ אִיּ֣וֹב שְׁמ֑וֹ וְהָיָ֣ה׀ הָאִ֣ישׁ הַה֗וּא תָּ֧ם וְיָשָׁ֛ר וִירֵ֥א אֱלֹהִ֖ים וְסָ֥ר מֵרָֽע׃

passages.text: He had seven sons and three daughters, and he owned 7,000 sheep, 3,000 camels, 500 yoke of oxen, 500 female donkeys, and a very large number of servants. Job was the greatest man of all the people of the East.
passages.sermon:
Job lived in the land of Uz.
Job had seven sons.
Job had three daughters.
Job owned 7,000 sheep.
Job owned 3,000 camels.
Job owned 500 yoke of oxen.
Job owned 500 female donkeys.
Job had a very large number of servants.
Job was greater than all the people of the East.
passages.original: וַיִּוָּ֥לְדוּ ל֛וֹ שִׁבְעָ֥ה בָנִ֖ים וְשָׁל֥וֹשׁ בָּנֽוֹת׃ וַיְהִ֣י מִ֠קְנֵהוּ שִֽׁבְעַ֨ת אַלְפֵי־ צֹ֜אן וּשְׁלֹ֧שֶׁת אַלְפֵ֣י גְמַלִּ֗ים וַחֲמֵ֨שׁ מֵא֤וֹת צֶֽמֶד־ בָּקָר֙ וַחֲמֵ֣שׁ מֵא֣וֹת אֲתוֹנ֔וֹת וַעֲבֻדָּ֖ה רַבָּ֣ה מְאֹ֑ד וַיְהִי֙ הָאִ֣ישׁ הַה֔וּא גָּד֖וֹל מִכָּל־ בְּנֵי־ קֶֽדֶם׃

passages.text: Job’s sons would take turns holding feasts in their homes, and they would invite their three sisters to eat and drink with them.
passages.sermon:
Job had sons and daughters.
His sons held feasts.
Each son hosted a feast in his own house.
They took turns hosting these feasts.
The sons invited their three sisters.
The sisters came to eat and drink with their brothers.
passages.original: וְהָלְכ֤וּ בָנָיו֙ וְעָשׂ֣וּ מִשְׁתֶּ֔ה בֵּ֖ית אִ֣ישׁ יוֹמ֑וֹ וְשָׁלְח֗וּ וְקָרְאוּ֙ לִשְׁלֹ֣שֶׁת אַחְיֹתֵיהֶם לֶאֱכֹ֥ל וְלִשְׁתּ֖וֹת עִמָּהֶֽם׃

passages.text: And when the days of feasting were over, Job would send for his children to purify them, rising early in the morning to offer burnt offerings for all of them. For Job thought, “Perhaps my children have sinned and cursed God in their hearts.” This was Job’s regular practice.
passages.sermon:
Job was a man who was blameless and upright.
He feared God and turned away from evil.
Job had seven sons and three daughters.
His sons often held feasts in their homes.
They invited their three sisters to eat and drink with them.
When the days of feasting ended, Job acted.
He sent for his children.
He purified them.
He rose early in the morning.
He offered burnt offerings for each of his children.
Job thought, “Perhaps my children have sinned in their hearts.”
He also thought, “Perhaps they have cursed God in their hearts.”
Job did this every time the feasting ended.
This was Job’s regular practice.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֡י כִּ֣י הִקִּיפֽוּ֩ יְמֵ֨י הַמִּשְׁתֶּ֜ה וַיִּשְׁלַ֧ח אִיּ֣וֹב וַֽיְקַדְּשֵׁ֗ם וְהִשְׁכִּ֣ים בַּבֹּקֶר֮ וְהֶעֱלָ֣ה עֹלוֹת֮ מִסְפַּ֣ר כֻּלָּם֒ כִּ֚י אָמַ֣ר אִיּ֔וֹב אוּלַי֙ חָטְא֣וּ בָנַ֔י וּבֵרֲכ֥וּ אֱלֹהִ֖ים בִּלְבָבָ֑ם כָּ֛כָה יַעֲשֶׂ֥ה אִיּ֖וֹב כָּל־ הַיָּמִֽים׃פ

passages.text: One day the sons of God came to present themselves before the LORD, and Satan also came with them.
passages.sermon:
The sons of God are heavenly beings.
One day, these heavenly beings came before the LORD.
They came to present themselves to Him.
Satan also came with them.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֣י הַיּ֔וֹם וַיָּבֹ֙אוּ֙ בְּנֵ֣י הָאֱלֹהִ֔ים לְהִתְיַצֵּ֖ב עַל־ יְהוָ֑ה וַיָּב֥וֹא גַֽם־ הַשָּׂטָ֖ן בְּתוֹכָֽם׃

passages.text: “Where have you come from?” said the LORD to Satan. “From roaming through the earth,” he replied, “and walking back and forth in it.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Satan.
The LORD asked Satan a question.
The LORD said, “Where have you come from?”
Satan answered the LORD.
Satan said, “I have been roaming through the earth.”
Satan said, “I have been walking back and forth in the earth.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֧אמֶר יְהוָ֛ה אֶל־ הַשָּׂטָ֖ן מֵאַ֣יִן תָּבֹ֑א וַיַּ֨עַן הַשָּׂטָ֤ן אֶת־ יְהוָה֙ וַיֹּאמַ֔ר מִשּׁ֣וּט בָּאָ֔רֶץ וּמֵֽהִתְהַלֵּ֖ךְ בָּֽהּ׃

passages.text: Then the LORD said to Satan, “Have you considered My servant Job? For there is no one on earth like him, a man who is blameless and upright, who fears God and shuns evil.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Satan.
The LORD asked Satan about Job.
Job is the LORD’s servant.
No one on earth is like Job.
Job is blameless.
Job is upright.
Job fears God.
Job turns away from evil.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֶל־ הַשָּׂטָ֔ן הֲשַׂ֥מְתָּ לִבְּךָ֖ עַל־ עַבְדִּ֣י אִיּ֑וֹב כִּ֣י אֵ֤ין כָּמֹ֙הוּ֙ בָּאָ֔רֶץ אִ֣ישׁ תָּ֧ם וְיָשָׁ֛ר יְרֵ֥א אֱלֹהִ֖ים וְסָ֥ר מֵרָֽע׃

passages.text: Satan answered the LORD, “Does Job fear God for nothing?
passages.sermon: Satan spoke to the LORD.\r\nSatan asked a question.\r\nSatan said, “Does Job fear God for no reason?”
passages.original: וַיַּ֧עַן הַשָּׂטָ֛ן אֶת־ יְהוָ֖ה וַיֹּאמַ֑ר הַֽחִנָּ֔ם יָרֵ֥א אִיּ֖וֹב אֱלֹהִֽים׃

passages.text: Have You not placed a hedge on every side around him and his household and all that he owns? You have blessed the work of his hands, and his possessions have increased in the land.
passages.sermon:
God protected Job.
God protected Job’s household.
God protected everything Job owned.
God surrounded Job and all he had with safety.
God blessed Job’s work.
God caused Job’s possessions to grow.
Job’s wealth increased in the land.
passages.original: הֲלֹֽא־ אַתְּ שַׂ֣כְתָּ בַעֲד֧וֹ וּבְעַד־ בֵּית֛וֹ וּבְעַ֥ד כָּל־ אֲשֶׁר־ ל֖וֹ מִסָּבִ֑יב מַעֲשֵׂ֤ה יָדָיו֙ בֵּרַ֔כְתָּ וּמִקְנֵ֖הוּ פָּרַ֥ץ בָּאָֽרֶץ׃

passages.text: But stretch out Your hand and strike all that he has, and he will surely curse You to Your face.”
passages.sermon:
Satan spoke to the LORD.
Satan challenged God about Job.
Satan said, “Reach out Your hand.
Strike everything that Job has.
If You do this, Job will curse You to Your face.”
passages.original: וְאוּלָם֙ שְֽׁלַֽח־ נָ֣א יָֽדְךָ֔ וְגַ֖ע בְּכָל־ אֲשֶׁר־ ל֑וֹ אִם־ לֹ֥א עַל־ פָּנֶ֖יךָ יְבָרֲכֶֽךָּ׃

passages.text: “Very well,” said the LORD to Satan. “Everything he has is in your hands, but you must not lay a hand on the man himself.” Then Satan went out from the presence of the LORD.
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Satan.
The LORD gave Satan permission.
The LORD said, “Everything Job owns is now in your power.
Do not harm Job himself.”
Satan left the presence of the LORD.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֶל־ הַשָּׂטָ֗ן הִנֵּ֤ה כָל־ אֲשֶׁר־ לוֹ֙ בְּיָדֶ֔ךָ רַ֣ק אֵלָ֔יו אַל־ תִּשְׁלַ֖ח יָדֶ֑ךָ וַיֵּצֵא֙ הַשָּׂטָ֔ן מֵעִ֖ם פְּנֵ֥י יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: One day, while Job’s sons and daughters were eating and drinking wine in their oldest brother’s house, a messenger came and reported to Job: “While the oxen were plowing and the donkeys were grazing nearby, the Sabeans swooped down and took them away. They put the servants to the sword, and I alone have escaped to tell you!”
passages.sermon:
Job was a righteous man.
He had sons and daughters.
One day, his sons and daughters were eating and drinking wine.
They were in the house of their oldest brother.
A messenger came to Job.
The messenger spoke to Job.
He said the oxen were plowing.
He said the donkeys were grazing nearby.
The Sabeans attacked suddenly.
The Sabeans took the oxen and the donkeys.
They killed the servants with the sword.
The messenger said, “I alone have escaped to tell you.”
passages.original: וַיְהִ֖י הַיּ֑וֹם וּבָנָ֨יו וּבְנֹתָ֤יו אֹֽכְלִים֙ וְשֹׁתִ֣ים יַ֔יִן בְּבֵ֖ית אֲחִיהֶ֥ם הַבְּכֽוֹר׃ וּמַלְאָ֛ךְ בָּ֥א אֶל־ אִיּ֖וֹב וַיֹּאמַ֑ר הַבָּקָר֙ הָי֣וּ חֹֽרְשׁ֔וֹת וְהָאֲתֹנ֖וֹת רֹע֥וֹת עַל־ יְדֵיהֶֽם׃ וַתִּפֹּ֤ל שְׁבָא֙ וַתִּקָּחֵ֔ם וְאֶת־ הַנְּעָרִ֖ים הִכּ֣וּ לְפִי־ חָ֑רֶב וָֽאִמָּ֨לְטָ֧ה רַק־ אֲנִ֛י לְבַדִּ֖י לְהַגִּ֥יד לָֽךְ׃

passages.text: While he was still speaking, another messenger came and reported: “The fire of God fell from heaven. It burned and consumed the sheep and the servants, and I alone have escaped to tell you!”
passages.sermon:
A messenger came to Job.
He spoke while the first messenger was still talking.
He said, “The fire of God fell from heaven.
It burned the sheep.
It burned the servants.
It consumed them all.
I alone escaped.
I came to tell you.”
passages.original: ע֣וֹד׀ זֶ֣ה מְדַבֵּ֗ר וְזֶה֮ בָּ֣א וַיֹּאמַר֒ אֵ֣שׁ אֱלֹהִ֗ים נָֽפְלָה֙ מִן־ הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם וַתִּבְעַ֥ר בַּצֹּ֛אן וּבַנְּעָרִ֖ים וַתֹּאכְלֵ֑ם וָאִמָּ֨לְטָ֧ה רַק־ אֲנִ֛י לְבַדִּ֖י לְהַגִּ֥יד לָֽךְ׃

passages.text: While he was still speaking, another messenger came and reported: “The Chaldeans formed three bands, raided the camels, and took them away. They put the servants to the sword, and I alone have escaped to tell you!”
passages.sermon:
Job was a righteous man.
Job lived in the land of Uz.
Job was very wealthy.
Job had many servants and animals.
Job suffered great loss.

While one messenger was still speaking to Job, another messenger arrived.
The new messenger spoke to Job.
He said, "The Chaldeans attacked."
The Chaldeans formed three groups.
They raided the camels.
They took all the camels away.
They killed the servants with the sword.
I am the only one who escaped.
I have come to tell you."
passages.original: ע֣וֹד׀ זֶ֣ה מְדַבֵּ֗ר וְזֶה֮ בָּ֣א וַיֹּאמַר֒ כַּשְׂדִּ֞ים שָׂ֣מוּ׀ שְׁלֹשָׁ֣ה רָאשִׁ֗ים וַֽיִּפְשְׁט֤וּ עַל־ הַגְּמַלִּים֙ וַיִּקָּח֔וּם וְאֶת־ הַנְּעָרִ֖ים הִכּ֣וּ לְפִי־ חָ֑רֶב וָאִמָּ֨לְטָ֧ה רַק־ אֲנִ֛י לְבַדִּ֖י לְהַגִּ֥יד לָֽךְ׃

passages.text: While he was still speaking, another messenger came and reported: “Your sons and daughters were eating and drinking wine in their oldest brother’s house, when suddenly a mighty wind swept in from the desert and struck the four corners of the house. It collapsed on the young people and they are dead, and I alone have escaped to tell you!”
passages.sermon:
A messenger came to Job.
Job was a righteous man who feared God.
The messenger spoke while another was still speaking.
He said, “Your sons and daughters were eating and drinking wine.
They were in the house of their oldest brother.
Suddenly, a strong wind came from the desert.
The wind struck all four corners of the house.
The house fell on the young people.
They died.
I alone escaped to tell you.”
passages.original: עַ֚ד זֶ֣ה מְדַבֵּ֔ר וְזֶ֖ה בָּ֣א וַיֹּאמַ֑ר בָּנֶ֨יךָ וּבְנוֹתֶ֤יךָ אֹֽכְלִים֙ וְשֹׁתִ֣ים יַ֔יִן בְּבֵ֖ית אֲחִיהֶ֥ם הַבְּכֽוֹר׃ וְהִנֵּה֩ ר֨וּחַ גְּדוֹלָ֜ה בָּ֣אָה׀ מֵעֵ֣בֶר הַמִּדְבָּ֗ר וַיִּגַּע֙ בְּאַרְבַּע֙ פִּנּ֣וֹת הַבַּ֔יִת וַיִּפֹּ֥ל עַל־ הַנְּעָרִ֖ים וַיָּמ֑וּתוּ וָאִמָּ֨לְטָ֧ה רַק־ אֲנִ֛י לְבַדִּ֖י לְהַגִּ֥יד לָֽךְ׃

passages.text: Then Job stood up, tore his robe, and shaved his head. He fell to the ground and worshiped, saying: “Naked I came from my mother’s womb, and naked I will return. The LORD gave, and the LORD has taken away. Blessed be the name of the LORD.”
passages.sermon:
Job was a righteous man who suffered great loss.
Job stood up.
He tore his robe.
He shaved his head.
He fell to the ground.
He worshiped God.
Job said, “I came from my mother’s womb with nothing.
I will return with nothing.
The LORD gave.
The LORD has taken away.
May the name of the LORD be blessed.”
passages.original: וַיָּ֤קָם אִיּוֹב֙ וַיִּקְרַ֣ע אֶת־ מְעִל֔וֹ וַיָּ֖גָז אֶת־ רֹאשׁ֑וֹ וַיִּפֹּ֥ל אַ֖רְצָה וַיִּשְׁתָּֽחוּ׃ וַיֹּאמֶר֩ עָרֹ֨ם יָצָתִי מִבֶּ֣טֶן אִמִּ֗י וְעָרֹם֙ אָשׁ֣וּב שָׁ֔מָה יְהוָ֣ה נָתַ֔ן וַיהוָ֖ה לָקָ֑ח יְהִ֛י שֵׁ֥ם יְהוָ֖ה מְבֹרָֽךְ׃

passages.text: In all this, Job did not sin or charge God with wrongdoing.
passages.sermon:
Job was a man who was blameless and upright.
He feared God.
He shunned evil.
Job suffered great loss and pain.
He lost his children.
He lost his possessions.
In all this, Job did not sin.
He did not accuse God of wrongdoing.
passages.original: בְּכָל־ זֹ֖את לֹא־ חָטָ֣א אִיּ֑וֹב וְלֹא־ נָתַ֥ן תִּפְלָ֖ה לֵאלֹהִֽים׃פ
